architecture.mechanism: Operating multiple magnetrons (7) simultaneously while rotating the load about its axis superposes electromagnetic fields from several sources and continuously moves the load through them, time-averaging the standing-wave pattern so energy deposits uniformly instead of at fixed hot spots.
architecture.intervention: Replace the single-magnetron, static-plate countertop oven with a cavity fitted with multiple magnetrons distributed around the chamber plus a turntable that rotates the food about its vertical axis for the entire cycle, requiring no mid-cycle stirring by the user.
architecture.expected_effect: Hot spots at food edges are eliminated and the center reaches target temperature, collapsing the surface-to-interior temperature gradient to approximately 1°C and yielding even heating throughout the load.
architecture.falsification_test: Heat a standardized agar food phantom of fixed geometry for one full cycle, then map surface temperature with a thermal camera and probe temperature at 1/4 depth; if any measured point deviates from the spatial mean by more than ~1-2°C, or edge temperature exceeds center by more than ~2°C, the mechanism is falsified.
